title: From Educational Innovation to Social Value: Developing a Reciprocal Dissemination Framework for School External Engagement and Social Impact
content: The transformation of schools into open, innovative and socially connected learning organizations has become a central concern in contemporary educational research. Educational innovation, however, does not automatically produce sustainable change or social value. Its impact depends on organizational capacity, collaborative networks, dissemination practices, and the ability to transform external interaction into organizational learning. This doctoral study further develops the Reciprocal Dissemination Framework for School External Engagement and Social Impact (RDF-SEEF), which conceptualizes school openness as a continuous, bidirectional exchange of knowledge, experience, feedback, resources, and opportunities between schools and their social environments.RDF-SEEF comprises four interconnected dimensions: School Innovation Capacity, School External Engagement, Reciprocal Dissemination Processes, and Social Value and Educational Impact. The framework will be empirically examined within one Model Junior High School as the bounded case of an embedded single-case study. The study will be quantitative-dominant and multi-stakeholder, using linked but stakeholder-specific questionnaires for leadership/teachers, students, parents/guardians, and external partners. Relevant school documentation will provide contextual corroboration. The purpose is not statistical generalization to all Model Junior High Schools but empirical examination and theoretical refinement of RDF-SEEF within a theoretically relevant real-world setting. Particular methodological and ethical safeguards will address the researcher’s dual role as both school Principal and principal investigator.
